summary: This is a Snowflake reference page for the JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY string function, which computes the Jaro-Winkler similarity between two strings as an integer from 0 (no similarity) to 100 (exact match). The comparison is case-insensitive but sensitive to all formatting characters, including whitespace. The page covers syntax, arguments, usage notes on execution time, collation behavior, and a worked example comparing several string pairs with their scores.
one_line: Reference page for Snowflake's JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY function, which scores string similarity from 0 to 100.
key_facts: JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY computes the Jaro-Winkler similarity of two input strings and returns an integer between 0 and 100.
A return value of 0 indicates no similarity, and 100 indicates an exact match.
The computation is sensitive to all formatting characters, including white space characters.
The syntax is JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY( <string_expr1> , <string_expr2> ), and both arguments are required.
When comparing short strings, execution time is proportional to the product of the lengths of the input strings.
When comparing long strings, execution time is proportional to the length of the longer string.
Collation details have no impact: in languages with digraphs or trigraphs such as Hungarian 'Dz' and 'Dzs', each character is treated as an independent character.
The result is based solely on the characters in the strings, not on the collation specifications of the strings.
In the example, 'Gute nacht' compared with 'Ich weis nicht' scores 56 in both directions.
In the example, 'Ich weiß nicht' compared with 'Ich wei? nicht' scores 98.
In the example, 'Ich weiß nicht' compared with 'Ich weiss nicht' scores 97.
In the example, 'Snowflake' compared with 'Oracle' scores 61.
In the example, 'święta' compared with 'swieta' scores 77.
In the example, comparing an empty string with an empty string scores 0, and comparing NULL with any string returns NULL.
